paper_title: An Overview of Thermal Challenges and Opportunities for Monolithic 3D ICs

scenario.figure_or_table: Section 3.1 text and Figure 4 (thermal maps of TSV-based 3D IC and Mono3D IC with four upper-tier hot spots and one bottom-tier hot spot)
scenario.description: Two-tier flip-chip Mono3D IC compared with a similarly sized two-tier TSV-based 3D IC in HotSpot-6.0. The 10 mm x 10 mm chip has one 400 um x 400 um hot spot at the center of the bottom tier and four 400 um x 400 um hot spots in the upper tier. Background power densities are 25 W/cm2 (bottom tier) and 30 W/cm2 (upper tier). Interconnects receive 5% of total tier power, 20% of which goes to the TSVs. Each hot spot has a power density of 750 W/cm2. Hot spot coordinates and per-block watts are not published.
scenario.architecture: Two-tier flip-chip Mono3D IC (thin tiers, ILD, MIVs not modeled) versus TSV-based 3D IC (4 TSV arrays of 5 mm x 200 um x 33 um, bonding layer), with the heat sink mounted on top of the bottom tier; 10 mm x 10 mm die
scenario.workload: Synthetic steady-state hot spot power-density maps (not an application workload); background plus hot spot power densities
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state; hot spots 750 W/cm2, background 25 W/cm2 (bottom) and 30 W/cm2 (upper); maximum on-chip temperature kept below 110 C; TSV-based upper-tier hot spots about 109 C, bottom tier about 38 C cooler; Mono3D hot spots about 77 C with a roughly 4 C difference between tiers

original_setup.solver: HotSpot-6.0 architectural-level steady-state thermal simulator (grid-based, with heterogeneous in-layer modeling used for TSVs; 100 x 100 grids per layer cited in Section 3.3), PDF page 4
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper is an overview and simulation study with no placement or floorplan optimizer in the selected scenario; floorplanning and partitioning optimizers are only discussed as related work or future opportunities (PDF pages 3 and 6-7).
original_setup.controller: None. No runtime thermal controller is used in the selected scenario; runtime task allocation and operating-mode control are mentioned only qualitatively as opportunities (PDF page 7).
original_setup.benchmark: Synthetic hot spot power-density scenario (PDF page 4, Section 3.1, Figure 4). The 10 mm x 10 mm two-tier flip-chip Mono3D IC is compared with a TSV-based 3D IC. There is one 400 um x 400 um hot spot at the center of the bottom tier and four in the upper tier, each at 750 W/cm2. Background power density is 25 W/cm2 for the bottom tier and 30 W/cm2 for the upper tier. Interconnects get 5% of tier power, 20% of which goes to the TSVs. This is not an application workload.

thermal_observable.location: Hot spot locations on the bottom tier of the two-tier Mono3D IC (approximate, from the text describing Figure 4c/4d). The upper-tier hot spot value for the TSV-based 3D IC is about 109 degC.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Approximate hot spot temperature read from steady-state HotSpot thermal maps (maximum or hot spot level), reported as ~77 degC in the text. The tier-to-tier variation in the Mono3D IC is about 4 degC, versus up to 38 degC in the TSV-based IC.

physical_mismatches.reason: 3D stacked two-tier Mono3D and TSV-based structure (thin tiers, ILD or bonding layer, vertical inter-tier coupling and heat sink on top of the bottom tier). A 2D single-layer Studio model cannot reproduce vertical inter-tier heat flow, the upper-tier vs bottom-tier temperature difference, or TSV and MIV effects.

The paper models TSV arrays (4 arrays of 5 mm x 200 um x 33 um) and metal layers 1-8 with interconnect Joule heating (5% of tier power, 20% of which to TSVs). A 2D Studio model has no equivalent interconnect or TSV heating.

Hot spot coordinates for the four upper-tier hot spots and the per-block watts are not published, so no complete same-scenario floorplan and power set exists. Only dimensions (400 um x 400 um) and power densities are given (hot spot watts could be derived as density x area, but positions are missing).

The cooling configuration (heat sink and heat spreader parameters, convection resistance, ambient temperature) is not specified in the paper, and the paper's heat path runs through the bottom tier. A Studio package with a different cooling stack would give different temperatures.
The paper's solver is HotSpot-6.0 with multi-layer heterogeneous grids. The Studio solver and its grid and material treatment differ, so temperatures cannot be compared numerically.
The selected scenario is steady-state only, with no transient power trace, controller, optimizer or reliability analysis. A transient one-row trace would be purely illustrative.

studio_assumptions: Any Studio run would be a separate illustrative 2D placement built from the published dimensions (10 mm x 10 mm die, 400 um x 400 um hot spots) and power densities, with generated coordinates kept distinct from paper-derived facts.

Studio's bundled package and material assumptions (default silicon, TIM, heat spreader/sink, ambient and convection settings) are used instead of the paper's HotSpot-6.0 stack, whose parameters are not published.
Power would be a one-row constant (steady-state) trace.
Studio results would not be numerically compared with the paper's ~77 degC and ~109 degC values.
No exact replication of the paper is claimed.
missing_inputs: Coordinates (x_m, y_m) of the four upper-tier hot spots and the bottom-tier center hot spot, as the paper only says center and, for other scenarios, quadrant centers.
Per-block power rows (named watts); only power densities are published (hot spot 750 W/cm2, backgrounds 25 and 30 W/cm2).

HotSpot configuration files, layer stack thicknesses and material properties, heat sink, heat spreader and ambient parameters (no linked code, config or repository was found; artifact_search_status checked_no_links).
Layer files (floorplan files per layer) and the power trace files used in HotSpot.
Exact numeric thermal map data for Figure 4 (only approximate values in the text; any digitized figure values would carry uncertainty).
No pinned packet assets are supplied (assets list is empty), so there are no RLPlanner or ATPlace2.5D files or thermal configs.
